name: King's Gambit
blurb: The most romantic 1.e4 opening: White gives up the f-pawn on move two for open lines and a fast attack. Sharp and risky, best for players who enjoy tactics.

ideas.e4: Takes a central square and opens lines for the queen and bishop.
ideas.e4 e5 f4: The King's Gambit. White offers the f-pawn to pull Black's e5 pawn away, open the f-file for the rook and build a centre with d4.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3: Develops and stops ...Qh4+, a check that would be awkward now that the f-pawn is gone.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4: The bishop aims at f7, the square only the king defends, while Black spends moves on pawns.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4 Bg7 h4: Attacks the g5 pawn, which is the one holding Black's extra pawn on f4.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6 d4: Against the solid ...d6, White takes the centre with two pawns and plans to win back f4 later.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 e5: Pushes the pawn to kick the f6 knight away from the centre.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5: Against the Falkbeer Countergambit, White simply takes the pawn Black offered.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5 e4 d3: Challenges the e4 pawn at once. That pawn cramps White, so trading it off frees the position.
ideas.e4 e5 f4 Bc5 Nf3: Against the Classical Declined, White develops. Taking on e5 right away would allow ...Qh4+.
